scenario.title: May 2024 Solar Storm · 14-Day Mission
scenario.description: A 14-day ARES-6 training campaign featuring the historical NASA solar-storm case study on Mars day 4.
scenario.historicalScope: The May 20, 2024 event on Mars day 4 is historical. The other 13 daily events are ARES-6 educational training simulations and are not a replay of Curiosity's actual mission timeline.

events.title: Let's prepare the food garden!
events.description: Your crew has arrived on Mars. Should you plant the first crops now, or save power and water for other jobs?
events.scienceFact: Plants need water, light, and nutrients — the things that help them grow. A greenhouse gives plants a place with the right conditions.

choices.label: Plant the first crops
choices.description: Spend 5 power units and 5 water units to plant food. The crops need two Mars days to grow.
choices.explanation: Your crops are growing. They need time before they are ready to harvest.

choices.label: Save power and water
choices.description: Keep your supplies for other important jobs around the outpost.
choices.explanation: You saved your supplies, but no food is growing in the greenhouse yet.

events.title: Dust is covering our solar panels!
events.description: A dust storm has left dust on the solar panels. Dusty panels make less electricity for the outpost.
events.scienceFact: Mars can have huge dust storms. Dust on a solar panel can block sunlight, so the panel makes less electricity.

choices.label: Clean the solar panels
choices.description: Spend 5 power units to clean the panels. They can make more electricity again.
choices.explanation: The panels are clean. They can now make more electricity each Mars day.

choices.label: Keep our power
choices.description: Save your electricity for other important equipment.
choices.explanation: You kept your power, but the dusty panels will keep making less electricity.

events.title: The robot rover found an interesting rock!
events.description: Your robot rover has found a rock that scientists would like to study. You can collect a sample or save power.
events.scienceFact: By studying Martian rocks, scientists learn how Mars changed over time and what the planet was like long ago.

choices.label: Collect a rock sample
choices.description: Spend 8 power units to study the rock and finish this science goal.
choices.explanation: Great work! Your crew has finished its rock research.

choices.label: Save our power
choices.description: Wait before studying the rock and keep the electricity for later.
choices.explanation: You saved power, but the rock research is not finished.

events.title: A powerful solar storm is reaching Mars!
events.description: Mission Control has received news of a major solar storm. Charged particles have reached Mars. Should your crew use extra shelter protection or save the water?
events.scienceFact: The Sun can send bursts of energy and tiny charged particles into space. When a strong burst reaches Mars, it can increase radiation at the surface.

choices.label: Move the crew into the radiation shelter
choices.description: Set aside 5 water units to add basic shelter protection. In this game, it lowers the radiation-risk points from this event.
choices.explanation: The crew has extra shelter protection. It lowers the game's radiation-risk points, not a real measured dose.

choices.label: Save the water
choices.description: Keep the water for the crew's normal needs. The shelter will not have extra protection for this event.
choices.explanation: You kept the water, but the crew has no extra shelter protection for this event.

historicalRecord.radFinding: Curiosity's Radiation Assessment Detector recorded the biggest radiation surge of its mission since the rover landed in 2012.
historicalRecord.doseExplanation: NASA estimated that astronauts standing near Curiosity during this event could have received about 8,100 microgray (8.1 milligray) — around 30 chest X-rays.
historicalRecord.scienceNote: This is NASA's estimate of a possible astronaut dose near Curiosity during the historical event. It is not a measurement of the ARES-6 crew and is not used as a game damage value.
historicalRecord.gameModelNote: ARES-6 uses a simple danger level and fictional risk points for this choice. The shelter option lowers those game points; it does not calculate a real astronaut dose.
historicalRecord.sourceTitle: NASA: Watches Mars Light Up During Epic Solar Storm

events.title: The habitat's air system has stopped!
events.description: The machine that keeps the habitat's air safe is not working. Fix it now, or use backup mode for one Mars day.
events.scienceFact: People need clean air to breathe. A Mars home needs machines to provide and manage safe air for the crew.

choices.label: Fix the air system
choices.description: Spend 6 power units to repair the machine that keeps the habitat's air safe.
choices.explanation: The air system is working again. The crew can breathe safely inside the habitat.

choices.label: Use backup mode
choices.description: Save power for now. The air system will still need to be fixed by the next Mars day.
choices.explanation: Backup mode gives the crew a little time. Fix the air system before another Mars day passes.

events.title: Should we grow more food?
events.description: The crew can start another crop cycle or save supplies. If the habitat's air system is still broken, fixing it is also important.
events.scienceFact: Growing food on Mars takes planning. Plants need water, power, light, and time before they are ready to harvest.

choices.label: Fix the air system
choices.description: Spend 6 power units to restore the habitat's air system.
choices.explanation: You repaired the habitat. The crew can use its air system again.

choices.label: Grow another batch of food
choices.description: Spend 5 power units and 5 water units to start another crop cycle. The crops need two Mars days to grow.
choices.explanation: New crops are growing. They need two Mars days before harvest. Make sure the air system is working too.

events.title: Study the environment around your outpost!
events.description: Your rover has gathered information about the land, air and conditions around the outpost. Study the results or save power for the remaining mission days.
events.scienceFact: Scientists study Mars's air, weather, soil, and radiation to understand what future explorers may face.

choices.label: Study Mars's environment
choices.description: Spend 8 power units to complete this science goal.
choices.explanation: Excellent work! Your crew has finished its study of the Martian environment.

choices.label: Save our power
choices.description: Keep your electricity for the remaining outpost missions.
choices.explanation: You saved power, but the study of Mars's environment is not complete.

events.title: The rover has found a promising icy area!
events.description: The rover has reached a cold, rocky area that may contain water ice below the surface. Your team can scan the ground or save power for later work.
events.scienceFact: Scientists have found water ice on Mars. Learning where ice is found helps planners choose places for future exploration.

choices.label: Scan the icy ground
choices.description: Spend 7 power units to study the area and complete the water-ice survey.
choices.explanation: The rover completed its water-ice survey. Finding possible ice is useful information, but it does not automatically add water to your supplies.

choices.label: Save rover power
choices.description: Keep your electricity for the remaining outpost missions.
choices.explanation: You saved power, but the water-ice survey is not complete.

events.title: The water recycler has stopped working!
events.description: The machine that cleans and reuses some of the crew's water has stopped. You can repair it or use an emergency water reserve.
events.scienceFact: Space missions reuse water carefully. Cleaning and reusing water helps reduce how much must be carried from Earth.

choices.label: Repair the water recycler
choices.description: Spend 6 power units to repair the system. It can recover 2 water units after the crew's daily use.
choices.explanation: The recycler is working again. It can recover a small amount of water after the crew uses its supplies.

choices.label: Use the emergency water reserve
choices.description: Add 14 water units from the stored emergency supply, but leave the recycler offline.
choices.explanation: The extra water gives the crew more time, but the recycler is still offline and will not recover water each day.

events.title: Another dust storm is approaching!
events.description: Dust is covering the solar panels again. The outpost will make less electricity until the panels are cleaned.
events.scienceFact: Mars has dust storms that can spread dust over large areas. Dust on solar panels can reduce the sunlight they receive.

choices.label: Clean the solar panels
choices.description: Spend 5 power units to clear the dust and restore normal solar generation.
choices.explanation: The panels are clean again and can make their normal amount of electricity.

choices.label: Wait for the storm to pass
choices.description: Save power now, but the dusty panels will keep making less electricity.
choices.explanation: You kept your power, but the dusty panels will make less electricity until they are cleaned.

events.title: The food garden needs another crop cycle!
events.description: The crew has used much of its stored food. The greenhouse can grow another batch, but planting needs power and water.
events.scienceFact: Growing food away from Earth takes planning. Plants need water, light, nutrients and time before they can be harvested.

choices.label: Plant another food batch
choices.description: Spend 5 power units and 5 water units to start a crop cycle. Food can be harvested after two Mars days.
choices.explanation: A new crop cycle has started. The greenhouse can provide more food after the plants grow.

choices.label: Save power and water
choices.description: Keep the supplies for the other outpost systems. No new crops will grow.
choices.explanation: You saved the supplies, but the greenhouse will not produce another food batch from this choice.

events.title: The rover has collected new air and dust readings!
events.description: The rover's instruments have recorded information about the thin air and dust around the outpost. Your crew can study the readings or save power.
events.scienceFact: Mars has a very thin atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide. Scientists study its air and dust to understand the planet's weather and environment.

choices.label: Study the atmosphere readings
choices.description: Spend 8 power units to complete the atmosphere study.
choices.explanation: Your crew has studied the atmosphere readings and completed the atmosphere science goal.

choices.label: Save the power
choices.description: Keep electricity for the remaining mission systems. The atmosphere study will remain unfinished.
choices.explanation: You saved power, but the atmosphere study is not complete.

events.title: Mission Control has sent another space-weather warning!
events.description: Mission Control has warned that space-weather conditions may raise radiation risk. Your crew can add extra shelter protection or save water.
events.scienceFact: The Sun releases energy and charged particles. Space-weather alerts help mission teams prepare, but a warning is not the same as a measured dose at the outpost.

choices.label: Add extra shelter protection
choices.description: Use 5 water units to add basic water-based shielding. It lowers the game's radiation-risk points for this warning.
choices.explanation: The shelter has extra protection. It lowers the game's fictional risk points, not a real measured radiation dose.

choices.label: Save the water
choices.description: Keep the water for the crew's normal needs. The shelter will not receive extra protection for this warning.
choices.explanation: You saved the water, but the shelter has no extra protection for this warning.

events.title: The mission is nearly over. Send your research to Earth!
events.description: Your crew has collected information from the outpost. Use the antenna to send the final mission report to Earth, or keep the remaining power in reserve.
events.scienceFact: Messages from Mars take time to travel to Earth. Mission teams plan carefully so that important results can be sent home.

choices.label: Transmit the final research report
choices.description: Spend 6 power units to send your mission results to Earth. A successful mission needs all four science goals and this final report.
choices.explanation: The final research report has been sent to Earth. Mission Control has received your outpost's science results.

choices.label: Keep the remaining power
choices.description: Save electricity, but the final report will not be sent to Earth.
choices.explanation: You kept the power, but the final report was not transmitted. The crew can finish the mission, but the report is incomplete.
